goal: Track every research idea while prioritizing implementable, informative experiments; do not claim all are completed until verified.
selection_rule: Select the first unfinished, unblocked item from earliest feasible wave, using the registry plus dependencies and evidence. Work on at most one substantive independent hypothesis at a time; checkpoint between agent runs.

stages.name: wave-1-diagnostics-and-low-cost-controls
stages.objective: Establish baseline/control fidelity, detect practical losses, and find inexpensive high-information improvements.
stages.evaluation: Unit tests and replay labels, then 20-game color-balanced screening; only finalists proceed to independent-seed full-clock trials.

stages.name: wave-2-information-and-inference
stages.objective: Isolate gains from observation-consistent action evaluation, posterior quality, selective search and delayed tactical risk.
stages.evaluation: Feature ablations, CPU-matched comparisons, complete 180+2 trials for plausible winners; avoid claiming significance from small matches.

stages.name: wave-3-game-theory-and-learning
stages.objective: Pursue advanced opponent reasoning, population robustness and learned corrections where evidence or compute budget justifies them.
stages.evaluation: Prefer offline validation and CPU-matched small ablations; document failures and resource barriers rather than forcing all to full tournament.

stages.name: wave-4-high-cost-and-final-integration
stages.objective: Evaluate expensive end-to-end learning only if feasible, then integrate independently verified improvements as a final candidate.
stages.evaluation: Report grounded improvements, negatives, confidence intervals, resource cost and full reproducibility; no official arena without authorization.
